original_question: For a compact Hermitian manifold (X, omega), define T(X, omega) as the infimum of integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n over smooth omega-plurisubharmonic functions phi. Determine whether T(X, omega) can be equal to 0 for some manifold.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question 30 (Tosatti): the open problem asking whether the infimum of the total Monge–Ampère volume over smooth ω-plurisubharmonic perturbations can vanish on some compact Hermitian manifold.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target very closely: it is about a compact Hermitian manifold (X, ω), it defines the same quantity T(X, ω) as an infimum of ∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n over smooth ω-plurisubharmonic functions φ, and it asks exactly whether this quantity can be 0 for some manifold. This is precisely the content of Question 30, not the neighboring Question 29 or Question 31.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient dimension parameter n should be made explicit as n := dim_C X.
The infimum is taken over φ ∈ C^∞(X) ∩ PSH(X, ω); writing the class explicitly makes the question fully stand-alone.
To be self-contained, ω-plurisubharmonic should be defined, e.g. for smooth φ by the condition ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 as a semipositive (1,1)-form.
The object is a compact Hermitian manifold in the Hermitian/non-Kähler setting of Section 4; this contextual scope is implicit in the draft.
The phrase “for some manifold” should be read as existence of some compact Hermitian pair (X, ω), not merely some underlying complex manifold with unspecified metric.
No extra normalization on φ (such as sup_X φ = 0) is imposed in the paper’s formulation; the draft leaves this implicit.
The integrand (ω + dd^cφ)^n is the top exterior power integrated over X; making this explicit improves stand-alone clarity.
refined_question:
Let (X, ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold, and set n := dim_C X. Define
T(X, ω) := inf { ∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n : φ ∈ C^∞(X) and ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 }.
Equivalently, the infimum is over smooth ω-plurisubharmonic functions φ ∈ C^∞(X) ∩ PSH(X, ω). Is it possible that T(X, ω) = 0 for some compact Hermitian manifold (X, ω)?
justification: The draft is targeting Question 30 exactly. In Section 4, the paper switches to the Hermitian setting and emphasizes that, unlike in the Kähler case, the total volume ∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n generally depends on φ. Section 4.1 first raises Question 29 about characterizing forms ω for which this total volume is actually invariant for all bounded ω-psh φ, and then immediately introduces Question 30 by defining T(X, ω) as the infimum of these total volumes over smooth ω-psh perturbations and asking whether T(X, ω) can be 0. The neighboring Question 31 defines a different infimum, cap(X, ω), over 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, so your draft is not targeting that problem. Because your draft reproduces the definition of T(X, ω) and asks whether it can vanish, the nearest official formulation is Question 30 itself.
